newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica minister wants to negotiate on oil margins.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica minister wants to negotiate on oil margins.

text.p: The South African government wants to negotiate with oil companies over an increase in wholesale margins, but will not renege on its promises, Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna said on Tuesday.

The South African Petroleum Industry Association (Sapia) has applied to government for a three cents a litre increase to restore the industry wholesale margin to 15 percent. The margin has been eroded to 8.7 percent by rising costs since the last increase in 1993.

Maduna acknowledged the oil companies had a reasonable case but said a margin increase would involve the politically unpalatable decision to increase the price of all petroleum products, including paraffin used by most urban poor.

Giving his first briefing to parliament's mineral and energy affairs committees, Maduna said Cabinet had balked at both options and had appointed a ministerial committee to review the situation and the pricing of petroleum products in general.

Under a "gentleman's agreement" between the former government and the oil industry, government was obliged to top up the profit margins of the oil companies if they fell below a certain level, he said.
"If you look purely at that agreement, indeed, the companies have been shabbily treated by government, I don't have to be convinced about that," Maduna said.
"The price should have been raised on January 1 and this was never done. The consequence of that is that, as at August, they were already owed 513 million rand."
He said he had prepared a memorandum for Cabinet on the issue, arguing government should negotatie with the companies.
"I wish to reassure these companies that there is no intention not to fulfill our obligations," Maduna said.
"We are not exhibiting any hostility towards them as investors either. All that is happening is that we are preparing our own position as government...to negotiate with them."

Maduna added he was also under "tremendous pressure" from various lobbies to deregulate the oil industry as a whole so that supermarkets could sell gasoline, more filling stations could be opened and refined product imported.
Policy papers on all these issues were now being prepared and should be released soon, Maduna said.
